doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: College life: no professional aspirations, major and Saturday classes
summary: Playing weekends at other colleges, an English major arranged to avoid Saturday classes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So at that point, did you have aspirations to be a professional musician?

No. Not at all. I was, you know I had learned, self-taught, learned the ukulele and guitar and I played for high school sing-a-longs and stuff like that. As I said, when I got here I had no idea there was a jazz band or that I would be spending most of my weekends away from Hamilton at other colleges out playing.
It was. It was extremely neat, and of course my college record probably reflects that. I did make it through here with my degree, but Lord knows I don’t know how. But it was a fun four years.

English basically. But this was another aspect. I don’t know if Hamilton still has Saturday classes, but back in those days we did. I avoided them like the plague. So I tried to organize my schedule so that I never had a class that met on Saturday. And this meant that I had to take some courses that weren’t really ones that I would have appreciated. And I didn’t stay within the bounds of English, I went history, music, French. So I had, you know, if you will, kind of a broad brush. Yeah I had a broad brush education. It worked because I didn’t have to go down to Cornell or someplace like that and get back at two in the morning and get up and go to class.
I think Phil talked about that, that he wasn’t quite so smart as to not have Saturday classes.
Well if you’re a pre-med student or if you’re in the sciences, you know, there’s no way around it as I recall. There was always — you’d either have a lab on Saturday or a class or something.
